text: Helium was discovered or first isolated in 1868.
The name helium comes from the Greek word helios, meaning the sun.
In 1868, French astronomer Pierre-Jules-César Janssen noticed a yellow line in the sun's spectrum while studying a total solar eclipse.
Lockyer and Frankland suggested the name helium for the new element.
Helium gas is used to inflate blimps, scientific balloons and party balloons.
Liquid helium is used in magnetic resonance imaging, known as MRI, in medicine.
Helium is combined with oxygen to make a nitrogen-free atmosphere for deep sea divers.
Liquid helium is used to study superconductivity and to make superconductive magnets.
The name lithium comes from the Greek word lithos, which means stone.
Johann August Arfvedson discovered lithium in a mineral called petalite.
Lithium is used to make special glasses and ceramics.
A lithium compound called lithium hydroxide is used to remove carbon dioxide from the air inside spacecraft.
Some lithium compounds are used in dry cells and storage batteries.
The name beryllium comes from the Greek word beryllos, meaning beryl, which is a gemstone in which beryllium is found.
In 1828, the French chemist Antoine-Alexandre-Brutus Bussy and, independently, the German chemist Friedrich Wöhler first separated beryllium.
Beryllium was once also known as glucinium, from the Greek word glykys for sweet, until IUPAC chose the name beryllium in 1949.
Beryllium is used to make windows for X-ray tubes.
Beryllium is used to make an alloy called beryllium copper, which is used for things such as springs and electrical contacts.
Beryllium is used in parts of the space shuttle, such as the windshield frame and brake discs.
Beryllium is used in things such as gyroscopes and computer parts.
Boron was discovered or first isolated in 1808.
The name boron comes from the Arabic word buraq, meaning "white".
Boron was discovered in 1808 by French chemists Joseph-Louis Gay-Lussac and Louis-Jaques Thénard, and independently by English chemist Sir Humphry Davy.
Boron compounds were known for thousands of years before the element itself was isolated in 1808.
Borax, a boron compound, is used in laundry products.
Boron compounds are used to make borosilicate glass.
A boron compound is used to make fiberglass insulation and a type of bleach called sodium perborate bleach.
Boron filaments are used in the aerospace industry because they are strong and lightweight.
The name fluorine comes from the Latin word fluere, meaning "flow" or "flux".
The Swedish pharmacist and chemist Carl-Wilhelm Scheele discovered fluorine in hydrofluoric acid in 1771.
The French chemist Ferdinand Frederic Henri Moissan was the first to successfully isolate fluorine, in 1886.
Fluorine compounds, such as sodium fluoride, are added to toothpaste to help prevent tooth decay.
Fluorine is added to city water supplies to help prevent tooth decay.
Hydrofluoric acid is used to etch glass, including glass used in light bulbs.
Crystals of calcium fluoride, also known as fluorite and fluorspar, are used to make lenses that focus infrared light.
Neon was discovered or first isolated in 1898.
The name neon comes from the Greek word neos, which means "new".
Neon was discovered by Ramsay and Travers in 1898.
Neon was discovered through the study of liquefied air.
The largest use for neon gas is in advertising signs.
Neon is used to make high voltage indicators.
Neon is combined with helium to make helium-neon lasers.
Neon is used in devices such as lightning arrestors and TV tubes.
The name aluminum comes from the Latin word alumen, alum.
In 1825, the Danish physicist Hans Christian Oersted isolated impure aluminum.
The German chemist Friedrich Wöhler first isolated pure aluminum in 1827.
Aluminum and aluminum alloys are used to make products such as cans, foils and kitchen utensils.
Aluminum is used in electrical transmission lines because of its light weight.
Aluminum can be deposited on the surface of glass to make mirrors.
Aluminum alloys are important in the construction of modern aircraft and rockets.
Silicon was discovered or first isolated in 1824.
The name silicon comes from the Latin words silex and silicis, which mean flint.
Silicon was discovered by the Swedish chemist Jöns Jacob Berzelius in 1824.
Crystalline silicon was first prepared by the French chemist Henri Sainte-Claire Deville in 1854.
Silicon crystals are used to make electronic devices such as transistors, solar cells and microchips.
Silicon dioxide is used to make glass and bricks.
Silica gel, a form of silicon dioxide, absorbs moisture and is used as a desiccant, which keeps things dry.
Silicone, a material that contains silicon, is used for things such as lubricants, electrical insulators and medical implants.
Phosphorus was discovered or first isolated in 1669.
The name phosphorus comes from the Greek word phosphoros, meaning "bringing light", because it glows in the dark.
Phosphorus was discovered in 1669 by Hennig Brand, a German merchant.
The Greek word phosphoros was an ancient name for the planet Venus when it appears before sunrise.
Some phosphorus compounds that give off light are used in fluorescent light bulbs and television sets.
A phosphorus compound called trisodium phosphate is used as a cleaning agent and as a water softener.
Calcium phosphate, a phosphorus compound, is used to make china and baking powder.
Phosphates are used to make special glasses, such as those used for sodium lamps.
Sulfur has been known since ancient times.
The name sulfur comes from the Latin word sulphurium and the Sanskrit word sulveri.
Sulfur was once called brenne stone, meaning combustible stone, and the word brimstone comes from that name.
In 1809, French chemists Louis-Joseph Gay-Lussac and Louis-Jacques Thenard proved that sulfur is an element.
Most of the sulfur that is produced is used to make sulfuric acid.
Sulfur is used in making phosphatic fertilizers.
Sulfur is used in the vulcanization of natural rubber.
Sulfur is used to make papers, including sulfite paper.
Argon was discovered or first isolated in 1894.
The name argon comes from the Greek word argos, meaning "lazy" or "inactive", because it does not combine with other elements.
Argon was discovered in 1894 by Sir William Ramsay, a Scottish chemist, and Lord Rayleigh, an English chemist.
In 1785, Cavendish suspected that argon was present in air.
Argon is used to fill incandescent and fluorescent light bulbs to prevent oxygen from corroding the hot filament.
Argon is used as an inert gas shield for arc welding and cutting.
Argon is used as a protective atmosphere for growing silicon and germanium crystals.
Argon is used to fill tubes such as photo tubes and glow tubes.
Potassium was discovered or first isolated in 1807.
Potassium was first isolated in 1807 by the British chemist Humphry Davy.
The name potassium comes from the English word "potash" or "pot ashes," because it is found in caustic potash.
The symbol K comes from the Latin word kalium, via the Arabic word qali for alkali.
The greatest demand for potash has been for use in fertilizers.
Potassium hydroxide is used to make soaps, detergents and drain cleaners.
Potassium chloride is used as a salt substitute.
Calcium was discovered or first isolated in 1808.
The name calcium comes from the Latin word calx, meaning lime or limestone.
The Romans made lime under the name calx, but calcium metal was not discovered until 1808.
Calcium carbonate, a compound of calcium, is used to make things such as white paint, toothpaste and stomach antacids.
Calcium sulfate, also called gypsum, is used to make dry wall and plaster of Paris.
Calcium is used in vacuum tubes as a getter, a material that removes trace gases.
Calcium can be combined with metals such as aluminum, copper and lead to make alloys.
Scandium's name comes from the Latin word scandia, meaning Scandinavia, where the mineral was found.
Scandium was discovered by the Swedish chemist Lars-Fredrik Nilson.
The Swedish chemist Per Theodore Cleve proved that scandium was the element eka-boron that Mendeleev had predicted.
Alloys of scandium and aluminum are used in some sports equipment, such as baseball bats, bicycle frames and lacrosse sticks.
Scandium oxide, also known as scandia, is used to make high intensity lights.
Scandium iodide is added to mercury vapor lamps so that their light closely resembles sunlight.
Mercury vapor lamps with added scandium iodide give light resembling sunlight, which is important for indoor or night-time color TV.
Titanium was discovered or first isolated in 1791.
Titanium was discovered in 1791 by the Reverend William Gregor, an English pastor.
The name titanium comes from the Latin titans, the first sons of the Earth in Greek mythology.
In 1795, the German chemist Martin Heinrich Klaproth rediscovered the element and called it titanium.
Because titanium does not react within the human body, it is used to make implants such as artificial hips and pins for setting bones.
Titanium oxide is used as a pigment to make white paint.
Titanium is used in parts of boats that are exposed to sea water, such as propeller shafts and rigging.
Titanium and titanium alloys are used in airplanes, among other things.
Vanadium is named after Freyja Vanadis, the Scandinavian goddess of love and beauty, because of its many beautiful multi-coloured compounds.
Vanadium was discovered by Andrés Manuel del Rio, a Spanish chemist, in 1801.
Vanadium was rediscovered in 1830 by Nils Gabriel Sefstrôm, a Swedish chemist, while he was analyzing samples of iron from a mine in Sweden.
Vanadium-steel alloys are used to make things such as axles, gears for cars, springs and cutting tools.
Vanadium is used in producing rust resistant and high speed tool steels.
A vanadium compound called vanadium pentoxide is used as a mordant, a material that permanently fixes dyes to fabrics.
Vanadium pentoxide is used in the manufacture of ceramics.
Chromium was discovered or first isolated in 1797.
The name chromium comes from the Greek word chroma, meaning colour, because chromium forms many coloured compounds.
Chromium was discovered in 1797 by the French chemist and pharmacist Nicolas-Louis Vauquelin.
Vauquelin isolated chromium in 1798.
Chromium is often plated onto other metals to form a protective and attractive covering.
Chromium is added to steel to harden it and to make stainless steel.
Chromium gives glass an emerald green color.
A chromium compound called chrome yellow has been used as a yellow pigment in paints.
Manganese was discovered or first isolated in 1774.
The name manganese comes from the Latin word magnes, meaning magnet, because the mineral pyrolusite has magnetic properties.
Manganese was isolated by Gahn in 1774.
Manganese is mixed into steel to make it easier to form and work with, and to make it stronger and more resistant to impact.
Manganese is used to give glass an amethyst color.
Manganese dioxide is used in dry cells.
Manganese dioxide is used as a drying agent in black paints.
The name cobalt comes from the German word Kobold, meaning evil spirits or goblins.
Cobalt was discovered by the Swedish chemist Georg Brandt.
Brandt was trying to prove that an unknown element, not bismuth, gave certain minerals the ability to color glass blue.
Cobalt compounds have been used for centuries to color things such as porcelain, glass, pottery and tile.
Alnico, an alloy of aluminum, nickel and cobalt, is used to make powerful permanent magnets.
Cobalt is used to make alloys, including ones for jet engines and gas turbines.
Nickel was discovered or first isolated in 1751.
The Swedish chemist Axel Fredrik Cronstedt discovered nickel in 1751, in a mineral called niccolite.
The name nickel comes from the German word Nickel, meaning "deceptive little spirit".
Miners called the mineral niccolite Kupfernickel, meaning false copper, because it looked like copper ore but no copper was found in it.
Nickel is used to make some types of coins and batteries.
Nickel can be electroplated onto other metals to form a protective coating.
Adding nickel to glass gives the glass a green color.
Nickel is used to make stainless steel and other alloys that resist corrosion.
The name zinc comes from the German word zink, whose origin is unknown.
In prehistoric times, zinc compounds were used for healing wounds and sore eyes and for making brass.
Zinc was rediscovered by Andreas Sigismund Marggraf in 1746.
In galvanization, objects that can corrode, such as iron nails, are given a protective coating of zinc.
Metallic zinc is used to make things including dry cell batteries and roof cladding.
Zinc sulfide is used to make things such as television screens and fluorescent light bulbs.
Zinc oxide is used in products such as paints, cosmetics and soap.
Gallium was discovered or first isolated in 1875.
Dmitri Mendeleyev proposed that gallium existed in 1871, based on gaps in his newly created Periodic Table of Elements.
Gallium was discovered spectroscopically in 1875 by the French chemist Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran.
The name comes from the Latin word Gallia, meaning France, and also from the Latin gallus, a cock, a translation of "Lecoq."
Gallium has been used to produce solid-state items, including transistors and light emitting diodes.
Gallium has found use in high temperature thermometers.
Gallium has been used to create alloys with low melting points.
Gallium trichloride was gathered to build the Gallium Neutrino Observatory in Italy, which studies particles called neutrinos.
Germanium was discovered or first isolated in 1886.
The name germanium comes from the Latin word germania, meaning Germany.
Germanium was discovered and isolated by the German chemist Clemens-Alexander Winkler in 1886.
In 1871, Dmitri Mendeleyev first proposed that germanium existed, based on gaps in his newly created Periodic Table of Elements.
Germanium is used to make transistors for electronic devices.
Germanium is used as a phosphor in fluorescent lamps.
Germanium is used in infrared optical instruments and infrared detectors.
Germanium is useful as a component of wide-angle camera lenses and microscope objectives.
Arsenic was discovered or first isolated in 1250.
The name arsenic comes from the Latin word arsenicium and the Greek word arsenikos, meaning "masculine" or "male".
Albertus Magnus, a German alchemist, is believed to have first identified arsenic in 1250.
Arsenic compounds were mined by the early Chinese, Greek and Egyptian civilizations.
Arsenic is added to germanium to make transistors.
Gallium arsenide can produce laser light directly from electricity.
Arsenic is used in bronzing.
Selenium was discovered or first isolated in 1817.
The name selenium comes from Selene, the Greek goddess of the Moon.
Selenium was discovered by the Swedish chemist Jöns Jacob Berzelius in 1817.
Berzelius first believed the material was tellurium, but he eventually realized it was a previously unknown element.
Selenium is used in devices that respond to light, such as light meters for cameras and copiers.
Selenium is used in solar cells.
Selenium is used to make a ruby-red color in glasses and enamels.
Selenium is used in xerography for copying documents.
The name bromine comes from the Greek word bromos, meaning stench.
The German chemist Carl Löwig first prepared bromine in 1825.
The French chemist Antoine-Jérôme Balard first publicly announced bromine in 1826, so the discovery is credited to him.
A bromine compound called silver bromide is used in photography.
Some bromine compounds are used to help purify water.
Some bromine compounds are used in flameproofing agents.
Bromine is used to make products including dyes, medicines and sanitizers.
Krypton was discovered or first isolated in 1898.
Krypton's name comes from the Greek word kryptos, meaning hidden.
Krypton was discovered in 1898 by Scottish chemist William Ramsay and English chemist Morris Travers while they were studying liquefied air.
Ramsay and Travers found krypton in what was left after liquid air had nearly boiled away.
Krypton is used in some types of photographic flashes for high-speed photography.
Some fluorescent light bulbs are filled with a mixture of krypton and argon gases.
Krypton gas is combined with other gases to make glowing signs that give off a greenish-yellow light.
Rubidium was discovered or first isolated in 1861.
The name rubidium comes from the Latin word rubidus, meaning deepest red, because of the two deep red lines in its spectra.
Rubidium was discovered in 1861 by the German chemists Robert Bunsen and Gustav Kirchhoff while studying samples of the mineral lepidolite.
Robert Bunsen isolated rubidium in 1863.
Rubidium is used in vacuum tubes as a getter, a material that combines with and removes trace gases from the tubes.
Rubidium is used as a part of photocells.
Rubidium has been used in making special glasses.
Because rubidium is easily ionized, it might be used as a propellant in ion engines on spacecraft.
Strontium is named after Strontian, a town in Scotland.
Strontium was first isolated by the English chemist Humphry Davy in 1808.
In 1790, Adair Crawford recognized a new mineral, strontianite, as different from other barium minerals.
Strontium is used in making color television picture tubes.
Strontium is combined with iron to make magnets.
Strontium carbonate, a strontium compound, is used to make certain kinds of glass.
Strontium has found use in refining zinc.
Yttrium's name comes from Ytterby, a village in Sweden where the mineral gadolinite was found.
Yttrium was discovered by Johan Gadolin, a Finnish chemist.
Gadolin first called the element ytterbium, after the mineral ytterbite.
Yttrium compounds are combined with europium to make the red phosphor used in color televisions.
Garnets made from yttrium and iron are used as microwave filters in microwave communications equipment.
Garnets made from yttrium and aluminum are used in jewelry as simulated diamond.
Yttrium can be used in laser systems.
Zirconium was discovered or first isolated in 1789.
The name comes from the Arabic word zargun, which means gold-like.
German chemist Martin Heinrich Klaproth discovered zirconium in 1789 while analyzing a mineral called jargon.
Swedish chemist Jöns Jacob Berzelius first isolated zirconium in 1824, but it was not pure.
Zirconium is used to make some types of surgical equipment.
Zirconium oxide, also called zircon, is used as a gem material.
Zirconium dioxide can withstand very high temperatures and is used to line the walls of high temperature furnaces.
Zirconium is widely used in nuclear reactors.
The name niobium comes from Niobe, a character in Greek myths who was the daughter of Tantalus.
The British chemist Charles Hatchett discovered niobium in 1801 in a black mineral from America called columbite.
Hatchett gave the new element the name columbium.
Niobium is commonly used to make jewelry.
An alloy of niobium and titanium can be made into superconductive wire, which is used to make superconductive magnets.
Superconductive niobium cavities are at the heart of a machine built at the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility.
Niobium is used in arc-welding rods for some kinds of stainless steel.
Molybdenum was discovered or first isolated in 1778.
Molybdenum was discovered in 1778 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele, a Swedish pharmacist and chemist.
The name molybdenum comes from the Greek word molybdos, which means "lead".
In ancient times, people used the word "lead" for any black mineral that leaves a mark on paper.
Some electrical filaments are made from molybdenum.
Molybdenum is mainly used as an alloying agent in steel.
Molybdenum disulfide, a compound of molybdenum, is used as a lubricant at high temperatures.
Molybdenum trioxide, a compound of molybdenum, is used to make enamels stick to metals.
Technetium was discovered or first isolated in 1937.
Technetium was isolated by Carlo Perrier and Emilio Segrè in 1937.
The name technetium comes from the Greek word technetos, meaning artificial.
Technetium was the first element to be produced artificially.
Technetium can be used as a medical tracer.
Technetium can be used to calibrate particle detectors.
Technetium can slow the corrosion of steel, but only in closed systems because it is radioactive.
The name ruthenium comes from the Latin word ruthenia, the old name for Russia.
Russian chemist Karl Karlovich Klaus discovered ruthenium in 1844 while analyzing the residue of a sample of platinum ore.
Osann thought he had found new metals in his sample, which he called pluranium, ruthenium and polinium.
Ruthenium is mainly used as an alloying agent.
Ruthenium is added to platinum and palladium to make them stronger.
Alloys of ruthenium with platinum and palladium are used in jewelry and in electrical contacts that must resist wear.
Adding ruthenium to titanium makes titanium more resistant to corrosion.
Rhodium's name comes from the Greek word rhodon, meaning rose, because dilute solutions of its salts are rose colored.
Rhodium was discovered in 1803 by William Hyde Wollaston, an English chemist.
Wollaston obtained rhodium from a sample of platinum ore that came from South America.
Rhodium is used in jewelry.
Rhodium is used to make electrical contacts.
Rhodium is used in catalytic converters.
Rhodium is mixed into platinum and palladium as an alloying agent to make them harder.
Palladium was discovered or first isolated in 1803.
Palladium was discovered in 1803 by William Hyde Wollaston, an English chemist.
Wollaston discovered palladium while analyzing samples of platinum ore that came from South America.
Palladium was named after the asteroid Pallas, which was discovered at about the same time.
Palladium is used to make things such as springs for watches, surgical instruments, and dental fillings and crowns.
Palladium alloys are used to make jewelry.
When palladium is alloyed with gold, it forms a material known as white gold.
A palladium compound called palladium dichloride is used in carbon monoxide detectors.
Silver has been known since ancient times.
The name silver comes from the Anglo-Saxon words seofor and siolfur, whose origin is unknown.
The symbol Ag comes from the Latin word argentum and the Sanskrit word argunas, meaning "bright".
Silver has been known since ancient times.
Sterling silver is used for things such as jewelry and silverware.
Silver has been used to make coins, although today other metals are usually used instead.
Silver is sometimes used in making things such as electrical contacts and printed circuit boards.
Silver nitrate is used to make photographic films and papers.
Cadmium was discovered or first isolated in 1817.
Cadmium was discovered and first isolated by the German physician Friedrich Stromeyer in 1817.
The name comes from the Latin word cadmia and the Greek word kadmeia, the ancient name for calamine, which is zinc carbonate.
While studying calamine, Strohmeyer noticed that some samples glowed with a yellow color when heated, while other samples did not.
Cadmium is used in rechargeable nickel-cadmium batteries.
Cadmium can be electroplated onto other materials to protect them from corrosion.
Cadmium sulfide, a cadmium compound, is a yellow powder that is used as a pigment.
Cadmium compounds are used in the phosphors of black and white televisions and in blue and green phosphors for color TV tubes.
Indium was discovered or first isolated in 1863.
The name indium comes from the word indigo, for the indigo-blue line in the element's spark spectrum.
Indium was discovered in 1863 by the German chemists Ferdinand Reich and Hieronymus Theodor Richter.
A brilliant indigo line in a sample's spectrum revealed that indium existed.
Indium is used with germanium to make transistors.
Indium can be used to make mirrors that reflect as well as silver mirrors but do not tarnish as quickly.
Indium is used to coat the bearings of high speed motors.
Indium is used to make electrical components such as rectifiers, thermistors and photoconductors.
Tin has been known since ancient times.
The name tin comes from the Anglo-Saxon word tin, and its origin is unknown.
The symbol Sn comes from the Latin word stannum, which was used for alloys containing lead.
Tin was known in prehistoric times.
Tin resists corrosion and is used as a protective coating on other metals.
Tin and lead are mixed together to make pewter and solder.
A tin compound called stannous fluoride is used in some types of toothpaste.
Antimony has been known since ancient times.
The name antimony comes from the Greek words anti and monos, meaning "not alone" or "not one", because it was found in many compounds.
The symbol Sb comes from stibium, from the Greek stibi meaning "mark", because it was used for blackening eyebrows and eyelashes.
Nicolas Lémery, a French chemist, was the first person to scientifically study antimony and its compounds.
Very pure antimony is used to make some semiconductor devices, such as diodes and infrared detectors.
Antimony is alloyed with lead to make the lead more durable.
Antimony alloys are used in products including batteries and cable sheathing.
Antimony compounds are used to make products such as paints, glass and pottery.
The name tellurium comes from the Latin Tellus, who was the Roman goddess of the Earth.
Tellurium was discovered in 1782 by Franz Joseph Müller von Reichenstein, a Romanian mining official.
Martin Heinrich Klaproth named the element tellurium but gave full credit for its discovery to Reichenstein.
Tellurium is used to color glass and ceramics.
Tellurium is added to copper and stainless steel to make them easier to machine and mill.
Tellurium is added to lead to increase its strength and its resistance to sulfuric acid.
A tellurium compound called bismuth telluride has been used in thermoelectric devices.
Iodine was discovered or first isolated in 1811.
Iodine was discovered in seaweed by the French chemist Bernard Courtois in 1811.
The name iodine comes from the Greek word iodes, meaning violet, because of its violet vapours.
The French chemist Louis-Joseph Gay-Lussac named iodine when he proved it was an element in 1814.
Iodine is used as a test for starch, because it turns deep blue when it comes in contact with starch.
A compound called potassium iodide is used to make photographic film.
Iodine compounds are very useful in medicine.
Xenon was discovered or first isolated in 1898.
The name xenon comes from the Greek word xenos, meaning "the stranger".
Xenon was discovered by the Scottish chemist William Ramsay and the English chemist Morris William Travers.
Xenon was discovered through the study of liquefied air.
Xenon is widely used in strobe lights.
The light from xenon lamps is used to kill bacteria.
Xenon ions were used as fuel in an experimental ion engine aboard a space probe.
Xenon gas is used in making electron tubes.
Cesium was discovered or first isolated in 1860.
The name cesium comes from the Latin word caesius, which means sky blue.
Cesium was discovered in 1860 by the German chemist Robert Wilhelm Bunsen and the German physicist Gustav Robert Kirchhoff.
Cesium was first isolated in 1882 by the German chemist Carl Setterberg.
Cesium is used in atomic clocks.
Cesium is used in photoelectric cells.
Cesium is used as a getter, a material that combines with and removes trace gases from vacuum tubes.
Barium was discovered or first isolated in 1808.
Barium was first isolated in 1808 by Sir Humphry Davy, an English chemist.
The name barium comes from the Greek word barys, meaning heavy.
In 1774, Scheele showed that baryta was different from lime.
Barium sulfate absorbs X-rays and, when swallowed, can be used to produce X-ray images of the intestinal tract.
Barium chloride is used as a water softener.
Barium ferrite is used to make magnets.
Barium carbonate is used in making ceramics and some types of glass.
Lanthanum was discovered or first isolated in 1839.
Lanthanum was discovered by Carl Gustaf Mosander, a Swedish chemist, in 1839.
The name lanthanum comes from the Greek word lanthanein, meaning "to be hidden" or "to escape notice."
It got this name because it hid in cerium ore and was difficult to separate from that mineral.
Lanthanum is used to make carbon arc lights, which the motion picture industry uses for studio lighting and projector lights.
Lanthanum is part of Misch metal, a material used to make flints for lighters.
Lanthana is used to make the glass in camera lenses and other special glasses.
Cerium was discovered or first isolated in 1803.
Cerium was named after the asteroid Ceres.
Cerium was discovered in 1803 by Berzelius and Hisinger, and independently by Klaproth.
Cerium is one of the rare earth elements used to make carbon arc lights, which are used in the film industry.
Cerium is part of misch metal, a material used to make flints for lighters.
Cerium oxide is a component of the walls of self-cleaning ovens.
Cerium oxide is used to polish glass surfaces.
Praseodymium was discovered or first isolated in 1885.
The name praseodymium comes from the Greek words prasios, meaning green, and didymos, meaning twin.
Praseodymium was discovered by Carl F. Auer von Welsbach, an Austrian chemist, in 1885.
Auer von Welsbach separated praseodymium, as well as the element neodymium, from a material known as didymium.
Praseodymium is part of misch metal, a material that is used to make flints for lighters.
Praseodymium forms the core of carbon arc lights, which the motion picture industry uses for studio lighting and projector lights.
Praseodymium salts are used to give glasses and enamels a yellow color.
Praseodymium is part of didymium glass, which is used to make certain types of welder's and glass blower's goggles.
The name neodymium comes from the Greek words neos, meaning "new", and didymos, meaning "twin".
Neodymium was discovered in 1885 by Carl F. Auer von Welsbach, an Austrian chemist.
Mosander named the element didymium because it was an inseparable twin brother of lanthanum.
Neodymium is added to glass to remove the green color caused by iron contaminants.
Didymium, which contains neodymium, is used to color glass for making welders' goggles.
Some neodymium salts are used to color enamels and glazes.
Glass containing neodymium can be used as a laser material.
Promethium is named after Prometheus, a figure from Greek mythology who stole fire from heaven.
The Czech chemist Bohuslav Brauner predicted in 1902 that promethium existed.
Jacob A. Marinsky, Lawrence E. Glendenin and Charles D. Coryell obtained proof that promethium exists in 1944.
Promethium could be used to make a nuclear powered battery.
Promethium could be used in generators that provide electricity for space probes and satellites.
Light made with promethium and a phosphor can be used for signs or signals that need to work dependably.
Promethium has applications as a source of beta radiation in gauges that measure thickness.
Samarium is named after the mineral samarskite, which was named for Colonel Samarski, a Russian mine official.
Samarium was originally discovered in 1878 by the Swiss chemist Marc Delafontaine, who called it decipium.
The French chemist Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran was the first to isolate samarium from the mineral samarskite.
Samarium, along with other rare earth elements, is used in carbon-arc lighting for the motion picture industry.
Samarium forms a compound with cobalt that is a powerful permanent magnet.
Samarium oxide has been used in optical glass to absorb infrared.
Samarium is part of misch metal, a material used to make flints for lighters.
The name europium comes from the continent of Europe.
Europium was discovered in 1896 by the French chemist Eugène-Antole Demarçay.
Demarçay suspected that samples of samarium, a recently discovered element, were contaminated with an unknown element.
Europium oxide, a compound of europium, is used as a red phosphor in television sets.
Europium has been added to some types of plastics to make lasers.
